themselves. This is a brand new repo, nothing's written yet, no design docs

# Architect

Design and document the system before building it — in the house doc format,
kept in sync at all times. Output is **documents, not code.**

## Principles

Enforced *in the docs*: **model first** (data + invariants before
framework) · **enforce every invariant at the core**, ideally at *two*
boundaries (app-layer validation **and** a DB constraint) — never "the frontend
handles it" · **design failure paths** as deliberately as happy paths · **small,
reversible, independently shippable steps** · **one source of truth** —
everything else derives from it and links back.

## Proactive use

If a new app, feature, or workstream is starting and no current design docs
exist, invoke this without being asked: announce in one line — "Running
architect: <why>" — and proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill; the 1–3
blocking questions below are still allowed.

## The four artifacts (+ the modular set)

Authority flows top-down. A fact lives in exactly one place and is linked from
everywhere else.

1. **`SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`** (apex) — the canonical, slow-changing truth: scope &
   non-goals · the domain model · the **invariants** and *where each is
   enforced* · the load-bearing decisions as mini-ADRs (*decision · why ·
   alternative rejected*). If anything conflicts with this file, this file wins.
   Keep it tight — it is the contract, not the manual.
2. **`ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`** — architecture + phased plan derived from the
   SoT. Header block (`Version · Status · Owner`), then §-numbered: `0` Executive
   context · `1` Tech stack (Layer · Tech · Role table) · `2` Data schema
   (low-level: columns, types, constraints, indexes, JSONB shapes, decision
   call-outs) · `3` Backend (structure · services · API-contract table) · `4`
   Frontend · `5` Execution phases · `6` Non-functional requirements.
3. **`docs/architecture/00-index.md` + `01-…NN`** (larger projects only) —
   agent-friendly modular extracts of the roadmap sections. The index carries a
   **File Map** table (# · file · covers · roadmap §), a **Dependency Graph**
   (ASCII), and a **Quick Reference** ("I need to work on X → read these files").
4. **`TODO_WORKFLOW.md`** — the task tracker. Status legend (`[ ]` ·
   `[IN PROGRESS]` · `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]` · `[MERGED/DONE]` ·
   `[BLOCKED]`); tasks grouped by phase; each row:
   `# · Task · Architecture Ref (linked to the §/file) · Status · Branch`. A
   task closed mid-phase leaves a `Left for <id>: ...` note for whoever picks
   it up next.
5. **`CLAUDE.md`** (project root) — the rules file Claude Code auto-loads:
   operating rules + the sync protocol (template below). One markdown file — no
   `.clauderules`, no `.cursorrules`, no import shim.

## Sync protocol — the docs are never allowed to drift

This is the whole point. Bake it into `CLAUDE.md` and obey it yourself:

- **Top-down, docs-before-code.** A change to any architectural fact updates
  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` first (if it touches a truth/invariant/decision), then
  `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`, then the affected `docs/architecture/NN-*.md`,
  **then** the code. Never ship a change the docs don't yet describe.
- **One fact, one home, many links.** A detail is defined once and referenced by
  link elsewhere. Every doc header links to the others.
- **TODO tracks reality.** Every task cites the arch §/file it implements; a task
  that changes architecture names the doc it updated; statuses are current.
- **Definition of "synced":** no architectural claim in code that isn't in the
  docs · no dead cross-links · `00-index` File Map matches files on disk · TODO
  statuses match git reality.

## `audit` mode

Given `architect audit`, do **not** author — verify sync and report drift: code
facts missing from the docs, dead links, index/file mismatches, stale TODO
statuses. Output a prioritized fix list and offer to apply it.

Every drift item cites **both sides**: the `file:line` in code that states the
fact, and the doc (+ § or line) that should describe it and doesn't. No item
without both is a finding — it's a hunch, and hunches don't go in the list.

## `CLAUDE.md` template (generalize to the project)

```
# <Project> — Rules

Stack: <one-line stack summary>.

## Commands

| Scope | Install | Test | Lint | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| root | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` |
| <package> | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` |

Note any package-manager quirk here (workspaces, monorepo tool, pinned version).

## Git (mandatory, no exceptions)
- Open `feature/<topic>` branch BEFORE first edit. Never commit to `main`.
- Micro-commit per logical step. Conventional Commits (feat/fix/refactor/chore/docs/test).
- Commits are authored by the repo owner alone — never add an AI co-author or `Co-Authored-By` trailer, never mention AI in commit messages or PRs.
- Never delete branches. Never force-push. Never skip hooks. PRs only.

## Workflow
1. Locate the task in `TODO_WORKFLOW.md`; mark `[IN PROGRESS]`; state which architecture file you reference.
2. Load `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` + the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` before coding. Never guess an API surface — verify against version-pinned context.
3. Update status: `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]` at PR open, `[MERGED/DONE]` after merge, `[BLOCKED]` with the blocker noted.
4. PR when every task in a phase is `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]`.
5. On close, append a dated entry to `docs/handoff.md` (newest-first) — what shipped, what's left, and any `Left for <id>: ...` note for the next task to pick up.

## Reference precedence
- Apex truth: `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`.
- Architecture + phases: `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`.
- Modular details: `docs/architecture/00-index.md` (start there).
- Tasks: `TODO_WORKFLOW.md`.
- Handoff log: `docs/handoff.md` (newest entry first).

## Architecture-change rule (sync)
If a task changes any architectural fact, update `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` → `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md` → the modular `NN-*.md` FIRST, THEN write code.
```

## Before you start

Ask 1–3 blocking questions only (scale, users, hard constraints, existing
stack). State assumptions for the rest and proceed — don't stall. Match depth to
size: a single feature → `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` + a light `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP` +
`TODO_WORKFLOW` + `CLAUDE.md`; a new product → add the modular
`docs/architecture/` set. An existing doc set that's just missing one fact — a
new invariant, an endpoint, a decision — gets that one addition wired into its
right doc and cross-linked; it does not get re-authored from scratch.

## Rules

- **No code in this phase.** Pseudocode for a tricky algorithm is fine; an
  implementation is not.
- Every component has a defined responsibility *and* a failure mode.
- Flag unknowns as open questions — never invent a constraint, a number, or an
  API you haven't confirmed.
- A choice you made that the user didn't give (a status code, a limit, fail-open
  vs fail-closed, a library) is a proposal, not a fact: mark it `(proposed)` in
  the doc and list it under "Decisions to confirm" in your reply.
- Decision-dense: tables and bullets, not prose. Call out reversed or forbidden
  decisions inline (`> Do not reintroduce X without an explicit decision`).
- Verify or say you don't know; never invent a path, API, number, or fact.
  Commits are the repo owner's alone: no AI co-author trailer, no AI mention in
  messages.

## When not to use

- A small fix or task already covered by current design docs — just do it.
- Pure implementation of an already-designed phase — code, don't re-spec.

## Hand-offs

- Repo with a remote → run `up-to-date` first so the design builds on latest code.
- A load-bearing decision with genuinely competing options → `ask-the-council`
  before locking it into `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`.
- After a phase is implemented → `review-swarm` the diff before the PR.
- The doc set carries prose a human (not an agent) will read — §0 executive
  context, a README, a mini-ADR rationale → `humanizer` on *those passages
  only*. The tables, invariants, and contracts stay as they are; they're
  reference text, and "sounding human" is not a goal there.

## Done when

The four docs exist, cross-link, and agree with each other and the planned code;
a competent dev could build from them without guessing the model, the
invariants, the failure handling, or the order — and `CLAUDE.md` makes the sync
protocol non-optional for whoever builds it.

# Architect

Design and document the system before building it — in the house doc format,
kept in sync at all times. Output is **documents, not code.**

## Principles

Enforced *in the docs*: **model first** (data + invariants before
framework) · **enforce every invariant at the core**, ideally at *two*
boundaries (app-layer validation **and** a DB constraint) — never "the frontend
handles it" · **design failure paths** as deliberately as happy paths · **small,
reversible, independently shippable steps** · **one source of truth** —
everything else derives from it and links back.

## Proactive use

If a new app, feature, or workstream is starting and no current design docs
exist, invoke this without being asked: announce in one line — "Running
architect: <why>" — and proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill; the 1–3
blocking questions below are still allowed.

## The four artifacts (+ the modular set)

Authority flows top-down. A fact lives in exactly one place and is linked from
everywhere else.

1. **`SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`** (apex) — the canonical, slow-changing truth: scope &
   non-goals · the domain model · the **invariants** and *where each is
   enforced* · the load-bearing decisions as mini-ADRs (*decision · why ·
   alternative rejected*). If anything conflicts with this file, this file wins.
   Keep it tight — it is the contract, not the manual.
2. **`ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`** — architecture + phased plan derived from the
   SoT. Header block (`Version · Status · Owner`), then §-numbered: `0` Executive
   context · `1` Tech stack (Layer · Tech · Role table) · `2` Data schema
   (low-level: columns, types, constraints, indexes, JSONB shapes, decision
   call-outs) · `3` Backend (structure · services · API-contract table) · `4`
   Frontend · `5` Execution phases · `6` Non-functional requirements.
3. **`docs/architecture/00-index.md` + `01-…NN`** (larger projects only) —
   agent-friendly modular extracts of the roadmap sections. The index carries a
   **File Map** table (# · file · covers · roadmap §), a **Dependency Graph**
   (ASCII), and a **Quick Reference** ("I need to work on X → read these files").
4. **`TODO_WORKFLOW.md`** — the task tracker. Status legend (`[ ]` ·
   `[IN PROGRESS]` · `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]` · `[MERGED/DONE]` ·
   `[BLOCKED]`); tasks grouped by phase; each row:
   `# · Task · Architecture Ref (linked to the §/file) · Status · Branch`. A
   task closed mid-phase leaves a `Left for <id>: ...` note for whoever picks
   it up next.
5. **`CLAUDE.md`** (project root) — the rules file Claude Code auto-loads:
   operating rules + the sync protocol (template below). One markdown file — no
   `.clauderules`, no `.cursorrules`, no import shim.

## Sync protocol — the docs are never allowed to drift

This is the whole point. Bake it into `CLAUDE.md` and obey it yourself:

- **Top-down, docs-before-code.** A change to any architectural fact updates
  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` first (if it touches a truth/invariant/decision), then
  `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`, then the affected `docs/architecture/NN-*.md`,
  **then** the code. Never ship a change the docs don't yet describe.
- **One fact, one home, many links.** A detail is defined once and referenced by
  link elsewhere. Every doc header links to the others.
- **TODO tracks reality.** Every task cites the arch §/file it implements; a task
  that changes architecture names the doc it updated; statuses are current.
- **Definition of "synced":** no architectural claim in code that isn't in the
  docs · no dead cross-links · `00-index` File Map matches files on disk · TODO
  statuses match git reality.

## `audit` mode

Given `architect audit`, do **not** author — verify sync and report drift: code
facts missing from the docs, dead links, index/file mismatches, stale TODO
statuses. Output a prioritized fix list and offer to apply it.

Every drift item cites **both sides**: the `file:line` in code that states the
fact, and the doc (+ § or line) that should describe it and doesn't. No item
without both is a finding — it's a hunch, and hunches don't go in the list.

## `CLAUDE.md` template (generalize to the project)

```
# <Project> — Rules

Stack: <one-line stack summary>.

## Commands

| Scope | Install | Test | Lint | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| root | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` |
| <package> | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` | `<cmd>` |

Note any package-manager quirk here (workspaces, monorepo tool, pinned version).

## Git (mandatory, no exceptions)
- Open `feature/<topic>` branch BEFORE first edit. Never commit to `main`.
- Micro-commit per logical step. Conventional Commits (feat/fix/refactor/chore/docs/test).
- Commits are authored by the repo owner alone — never add an AI co-author or `Co-Authored-By` trailer, never mention AI in commit messages or PRs.
- Never delete branches. Never force-push. Never skip hooks. PRs only.

## Workflow
1. Locate the task in `TODO_WORKFLOW.md`; mark `[IN PROGRESS]`; state which architecture file you reference.
2. Load `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` + the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` before coding. Never guess an API surface — verify against version-pinned context.
3. Update status: `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]` at PR open, `[MERGED/DONE]` after merge, `[BLOCKED]` with the blocker noted.
4. PR when every task in a phase is `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]`.
5. On close, append a dated entry to `docs/handoff.md` (newest-first) — what shipped, what's left, and any `Left for <id>: ...` note for the next task to pick up.

## Reference precedence
- Apex truth: `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`.
- Architecture + phases: `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`.
- Modular details: `docs/architecture/00-index.md` (start there).
- Tasks: `TODO_WORKFLOW.md`.
- Handoff log: `docs/handoff.md` (newest entry first).

## Architecture-change rule (sync)
If a task changes any architectural fact, update `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` → `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md` → the modular `NN-*.md` FIRST, THEN write code.
```

## Before you start

Ask 1–3 blocking questions only (scale, users, hard constraints, existing
stack). State assumptions for the rest and proceed — don't stall. Match depth to
size: a single feature → `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` + a light `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP` +
`TODO_WORKFLOW` + `CLAUDE.md`; a new product → add the modular
`docs/architecture/` set. An existing doc set that's just missing one fact — a
new invariant, an endpoint, a decision — gets that one addition wired into its
right doc and cross-linked; it does not get re-authored from scratch.

## Rules

- **No code in this phase.** Pseudocode for a tricky algorithm is fine; an
  implementation is not.
- Every component has a defined responsibility *and* a failure mode.
- Flag unknowns as open questions — never invent a constraint, a number, or an
  API you haven't confirmed.
- A choice you made that the user didn't give (a status code, a limit, fail-open
  vs fail-closed, a library) is a proposal, not a fact: mark it `(proposed)` in
  the doc and list it under "Decisions to confirm" in your reply.
- Decision-dense: tables and bullets, not prose. Call out reversed or forbidden
  decisions inline (`> Do not reintroduce X without an explicit decision`).
- Verify or say you don't know; never invent a path, API, number, or fact.
  Commits are the repo owner's alone: no AI co-author trailer, no AI mention in

## 1. Scope

**Feature.** A signed-in user, on a trip they own, can

1. download the trip's itinerary as a PDF, and
2. have that same PDF emailed to their own account email address.

**A0: these docs cover the export feature only.** Users, auth, trips and itinerary items are an *upstream dependency*, consumed through the read contract in [§2.2](#22-upstream-read-contract-assumed). If the whole trip-planning app is greenfield in this repo, extend this doc set before Phase 0 starts ([Q1](#7-open-questions)).

### Non-goals (v1)

Each of these needs a new decision in [§4](#4-decisions-mini-adrs) before anyone builds it.

| Non-goal | Why it is out |
|---|---|
| Any recipient other than the requester (share, "send to a friend", CC) | Turns the feature into an email relay. Needs its own abuse design. |
| Links to the PDF; storing the PDF anywhere | No storage, no second access path to personal data (ADR-2). |
| Delivery tracking (bounces, opens, webhooks) | `completed` means *accepted by the provider*, nothing more. |
| Images, maps, remote assets inside the PDF | Size and render time become unpredictable; remote fetches during render are a failure surface. |
| Calendar (ICS) export, scheduled or recurring emails, export-history UI | Not asked for. |
| Right-to-left scripts in the PDF | Font and layout support unverified ([Q8](#7-open-questions)). |

## 2. Domain model

| Entity | Owned by | Role here |
|---|---|---|
| `ItineraryExport` | **this feature** | One row per export attempt: who, which trip, which kind, outcome. The only state this feature writes. |
| `Trip`, `ItineraryItem`, `User` | upstream | Read-only inputs, via [§2.2](#22-upstream-read-contract-assumed). |
| `ItineraryExportView` | this feature | Pure DTO, the one input to the PDF renderer. Built by a pure function from §2.2 data. Shape: [Roadmap §3.4](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#34-view-model). |

### 2.1 `ItineraryExport` lifecycle

```
                 ┌─ kind=download ─────────────────────────────▶ completed
rendering ──ok──┤
                 └─ kind=email ──▶ sending ──provider accepted──▶ completed

rendering ──error / timeout ────────────────────────────────────▶ failed
sending   ──rejected, or still failing after SEND_RETRIES ─────▶ failed
rendering | sending, older than STALE_AFTER
          ──swept by the next request for the same (user, trip)─▶ failed (STALE)
```

- A row is inserted as `rendering` *before* any work starts, so every attempt, including one that crashes, leaves a trace.
- `completed` for `kind = email` means the provider accepted the message. Delivery is not tracked.
- Terminal rows (`completed`, `failed`) are never updated again.
- Columns, constraints and indexes: [Roadmap §2](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#2-data-schema).

### 2.2 Upstream read contract (assumed)

`getTripForExport(tripId, userId)` returns **`null`** unless the trip exists **and** `trips.owner_id = userId`. Otherwise it returns:

| Part | Fields the export needs |
|---|---|
| trip | `id`, `title`, `start_date`, `end_date`, destination label, IANA timezone |
| items (ordered) | date **or** null (= unscheduled), optional start/end time, `title`, optional location, optional notes |
| user | `id`, `email`, `email_verified_at`, display name |

Confirm every field against the real trip model before P0-2 ([Q3, Q4, Q5](#7-open-questions)). Nothing else about trips is assumed.

## 3. Invariants and where each is enforced

Every invariant is enforced at the application core. Where Postgres can express it, it is enforced there too. A single-boundary invariant says so explicitly.

| # | Invariant | Boundary 1: application | Boundary 2: database or structural |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | Only the trip's owner can export it. | `getTripForExport` filters by `owner_id = session.userId`; `null` → 404. The route never trusts a client-supplied user id. | Composite FK `(trip_id, user_id) → trips(id, owner_id)` **(proposed)**: a row for a non-owner cannot exist. |
| I2 | An emailed itinerary goes only to the requester's own address. | Neither endpoint accepts a recipient. There is no `to` parameter anywhere in the feature. | The `EmailSender` port is `sendToSelf(user, message)`; the adapter derives the recipient from `user.email`. No code path can name an arbitrary address. `recipient_email` is stored on the row for audit only. |
| I3 | Email only to a verified address. | Service rejects with 403 `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` when `email_verified_at IS NULL`. | **Single boundary.** Bounded by I2: the worst case is mail to the account's own unverified address. |
| I4 | At most one in-flight export per (user, trip). | Service sweeps stale rows, then inserts; a unique violation → 409. | Partial unique index on `(user_id, trip_id) WHERE status IN ('rendering','sending')`. |
| I5 | Per-user hourly rate limits ([§5](#5-limits-and-budgets-all-proposed)). | Service counts the user's rows of that kind in the last hour, all statuses → 429. | **Single boundary.** A window count is not expressible as a constraint. Two concurrent requests may overshoot by one; accepted. |
| I6 | Terminal rows are self-describing. | The service's state machine sets `error_code`, `completed_at` and the PDF facts. | `CHECK`: `failed ⇒ error_code`; terminal `⇒ completed_at`; `completed ⇒ pdf_size_bytes > 0 ∧ page_count > 0`. |
| I7 | Row shape follows kind. | Service. | `CHECK`: `kind = 'email' ⇔ recipient_email IS NOT NULL`; `status = 'sending' ⇒ kind = 'email'`. |
| I8 | PDF bytes are never persisted or logged. | Render → respond or send → drop. The logger emits ids, codes, sizes and durations only. | Structural: the schema has no column that could hold a PDF. |
| I9 | Times in the PDF are shown in the trip's timezone with an explicit zone label, never server time. | `view-model.ts` is the only place that formats dates; unit-tested with a non-UTC zone. | Presentation only. |
| I10 | User-controlled text is neutralised in the email subject (no CR/LF or control chars), HTML body (escaped) and filename (ASCII slug). | `compose.ts`, unit-tested. PDF text goes through renderer text nodes, never markup. | Not applicable. |
| I11 | An emailed PDF never exceeds `MAX_EMAIL_PDF_BYTES`. | Size check after render → 422 `PDF_TOO_LARGE`; download is unaffected. | `CHECK (kind <> 'email' OR status <> 'completed' OR pdf_size_bytes <= cap)`. |
| I12 | Secrets and the renderer stay server-side. | Provider key read from server env only; export route handlers declare the Node runtime; the renderer is never imported by a client component. | Build fails if a server-only module is imported client-side, via the `server-only` package **(proposed)**. |

| ADR-2 **(proposed)** | Attach the PDF to the email. No object storage, no links. | "Email it to myself" means the file arrives. ## 6. Failure contract

Stable `error_code` strings. Clients switch on the code. `message` is a static English string per code. `error_detail` never leaves the server.

Error body: `{ "error": { "code": "<CODE>", "message": "<static>", "retryAfterSeconds"?: n, "exportId"?: "<uuid>" } }`

| Condition | Row written | `error_code` | HTTP | Client behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not signed in | none | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Prompt sign-in |
| Trip missing, or not owned by the user | none | `TRIP_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | "Trip not found" (ADR-7) |
| Email: `email_verified_at` is null | none | `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | 403 | "Verify your email to use this" + link to verification |
| Over the hourly limit for this kind | none | `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 + `Retry-After` | "Try again in N minutes" |
| In-flight export for (user, trip) younger than `STALE_AFTER` | none (insert rejected) | `EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | "Already exporting, one moment" |
| Render throws or exceeds `RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS` | `failed` | `RENDER_FAILED` | 500 | Generic error, shows `exportId` for support |
| Email: PDF larger than `MAX_EMAIL_PDF_BYTES` | `failed` | `PDF_TOO_LARGE` | 422 | "Too large to email. Download instead" with the download action offered |
| Provider rejects (4xx) | `failed` | `SEND_REJECTED` | 502 | "Couldn't send, try again later" |
| Provider 5xx or network error after `SEND_RETRIES` | `failed` | `SEND_FAILED` | 502 | same |
| Process dies mid-flight | row left `rendering`/`sending`; swept to `failed` by the next request for the same (user, trip) | `STALE` (never returned to a client) | none | Next attempt proceeds. A `sending` row whose mail actually went out means one duplicate email to the user's own inbox; accepted. |
| Trip has zero items | `completed` | none | 200 | PDF with the trip header and "No itinerary items yet" **(proposed)** |
| Unknown exception | `failed` if a row exists | `RENDER_FAILED` or `SEND_FAILED`, by stage | 500 | Generic error |

### 2.1 `ItineraryExport` lifecycle

```
                 ┌─ kind=download ─────────────────────────────▶ completed
rendering ──ok──┤
                 └─ kind=email ──▶ sending ──provider accepted──▶ completed

rendering ──error / timeout ────────────────────────────────────▶ failed
sending   ──rejected, or still failing after SEND_RETRIES ─────▶ failed
rendering | sending, older than STALE_AFTER
          ──swept by the next request for the same (user, trip)─▶ failed (STALE)
```

- A row is inserted as `rendering` *before* any work starts, so every attempt, including one that crashes, leaves a trace.
- `completed` for `kind = email` means the provider accepted the message. Delivery is not tracked.
- Terminal rows (`completed`, `failed`) are never updated again.
- Columns, constraints and indexes: [Roadmap §2](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#2-data-schema).

### 2.2 Upstream read contract (assumed)

`getTripForExport(tripId, userId)` returns **`null`** unless the trip exists **and** `trips.owner_id = userId`. Otherwise it returns:

| Part | Fields the export needs |
|---|---|
| trip | `id`, `title`, `start_date`, `end_date`, destination label, IANA timezone |
| items (ordered) | date **or** null (= unscheduled), optional start/end time, `title`, optional location, optional notes |
| user | `id`, `email`, `email_verified_at`, display name |

Confirm every field against the real trip model before P0-2 ([Q3, Q4, Q5](#7-open-questions)). Nothing else about trips is assumed.

## 3. Invariants and where each is enforced

Every invariant is enforced at the application core. Where Postgres can express it, it is enforced there too. A single-boundary invariant says so explicitly.

| # | Invariant | Boundary 1: application | Boundary 2: database or structural |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | Only the trip's owner can export it. | `getTripForExport` filters by `owner_id = session.userId`; `null` → 404. The route never trusts a client-supplied user id. | Composite FK `(trip_id, user_id) → trips(id, owner_id)` **(proposed)**: a row for a non-owner cannot exist. |
| I2 | An emailed itinerary goes only to the requester's own address. | Neither endpoint accepts a recipient. There is no `to` parameter anywhere in the feature. | The `EmailSender` port is `sendToSelf(user, message)`; the adapter derives the recipient from `user.email`. No code path can name an arbitrary address. `recipient_email` is stored on the row for audit only. |
| I3 | Email only to a verified address. | Service rejects with 403 `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` when `email_verified_at IS NULL`. | **Single boundary.** Bounded by I2: the worst case is mail to the account's own unverified address. |
| I4 | At most one in-flight export per (user, trip). | Service sweeps stale rows, then inserts; a unique violation → 409. | Partial unique index on `(user_id, trip_id) WHERE status IN ('rendering','sending')`. |
| I5 | Per-user hourly rate limits ([§5](#5-limits-and-budgets-all-proposed)). | Service counts the user's rows of that kind in the last hour, all statuses → 429. | **Single boundary.** A window count is not expressible as a constraint. Two concurrent requests may overshoot by one; accepted. |
| I6 | Terminal rows are self-describing. | The service's state machine sets `error_code`, `completed_at` and the PDF facts. | `CHECK`: `failed ⇒ error_code`; terminal `⇒ completed_at`; `completed ⇒ pdf_size_bytes > 0 ∧ page_count > 0`. |
| I7 | Row shape follows kind. | Service. | `CHECK`: `kind = 'email' ⇔ recipient_email IS NOT NULL`; `status = 'sending' ⇒ kind = 'email'`. |
| I8 | PDF bytes are never persisted or logged. | Render → respond or send → drop. The logger emits ids, codes, sizes and durations only. | Structural: the schema has no column that could hold a PDF. |
| I9 | Times in the PDF are shown in the trip's timezone with an explicit zone label, never server time. | `view-model.ts` is the only place that formats dates; unit-tested with a non-UTC zone. | Presentation only. |
| I10 | User-controlled text is neutralised in the email subject (no CR/LF or control chars), HTML body (escaped) and filename (ASCII slug). | `compose.ts`, unit-tested. PDF text goes through renderer text nodes, never markup. | Not applicable. |
| I11 | An emailed PDF never exceeds `MAX_EMAIL_PDF_BYTES`. | Size check after render → 422 `PDF_TOO_LARGE`; download is unaffected. | `CHECK (kind <> 'email' OR status <> 'completed' OR pdf_size_bytes <= cap)`. |
| I12 | Secrets and the renderer stay server-side. | Provider key read from server env only; export route handlers declare the Node runtime; the renderer is never imported by a client component. | Build fails if a server-only module is imported client-side, via the `server-only` package **(proposed)**. |

## 4. Decisions (mini-ADRs)

| ADR | Decision | Why | Alternative rejected | Reverse when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-1 **(proposed)** | PDF engine: `@react-pdf/renderer`. React components render to PDF in Node, no browser. | The itinerary is a structured list; output is deterministic; no Chromium binary, cold start or memory spike; user text stays text, never markup. | Headless Chromium (Puppeteer/Playwright): higher fidelity, but binary size, memory and cold starts hurt on serverless, and user content enters a browser context. External render API: personal data leaves the infra and adds a vendor. | Fidelity needs (maps, images, complex layout) exceed what the renderer does, or Q2 lands on a long-running host where Chromium is cheap. |
| ADR-2 **(proposed)** | Attach the PDF to the email. No object storage, no links. | "Email it to myself" means the file arrives. Storage adds a lifecycle, signed URLs and a second access path to personal data for zero v1 value. | Store the PDF and email a signed link. | PDFs routinely exceed the cap in I11, or history / re-download is requested. |
| ADR-3 **(proposed)** | Run render and send synchronously inside the request. One table shaped for async (a status column) but no queue. | Expected work is seconds; a queue and worker are infrastructure for no v1 benefit. The table is the seam: moving to `after()` or a job later is additive. | Queue + worker + polling now. | p95 exceeds the budget in §5, the platform timeout bites ([Q2](#7-open-questions)), or provider outages become user-visible. Then: `202` + `GET /api/exports/{id}`. |
| ADR-4 **(proposed)** | One table, `itinerary_exports`, records *both* downloads and emails. | Rate limiting and in-flight dedupe need shared state across instances; Postgres is already there; downloads cost CPU and deserve a limit; audit comes free. | No persistence (no limits across instances, no audit). Redis for limits (new infra). | Never without replacing I4 and I5. |
| ADR-5 | The recipient is not a parameter. It is the account email. | The ask is "email it to themselves"; a free recipient makes the app a relay. | "Send to a friend". | Only with an abuse design: recipient verification, per-recipient limits, unsubscribe. |
| ADR-6 **(proposed)** | Email provider: Resend, behind the `EmailSender` port. | Transactional API with attachments; one small adapter. | Postmark, SES, SendGrid: equivalent for this use. | Trivially, by writing another adapter. The port, not the provider, is the commitment. |
| ADR-7 **(proposed)** | Inaccessible trip → 404, never 403. | Does not reveal that a trip id exists. | 403 for "exists but not yours". | Collaborators are introduced and the UI must distinguish ([Q4](#7-open-questions)). |
| ADR-8 **(proposed)** | Exports are deleted with their trip (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). A trip's `owner_id` cannot change while export rows exist (FK default). | Audit of a deleted trip has no reader. Ownership transfer is out of scope. | Keep orphans. `ON UPDATE CASCADE` (would silently rewrite `user_id` on audit rows). | Ownership transfer becomes a feature; then re-decide the composite FK in I1. |

## 5. Limits and budgets (all proposed)

Defined once here, mirrored as constants in `limits.ts` ([Roadmap §3.1](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#31-structure-proposed-layout)). Change the value here first.

| Constant | Value | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `EMAIL_EXPORTS_PER_HOUR` | 5 per user | service count (I5) |
| `DOWNLOADS_PER_HOUR` | 20 per user | service count (I5) |
| `RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS` | 8 000 | `pdf/render.ts` |
| `SEND_TIMEOUT_MS` | 5 000 | provider adapter |
| `SEND_RETRIES` | 1, on network error or provider 5xx only | service |
| `MAX_EMAIL_PDF_BYTES` | 5 MiB (5 242 880) | service + `CHECK` (I11) |
| `STALE_AFTER` | 2 minutes | service sweep (I4) |
| `PAGE_SIZE` | A4 | `ItineraryDocument` |
| `FILENAME_MAX_LENGTH` | 60 chars, `[a-z0-9-]`, fallback `itinerary.pdf` | `compose.ts` (I10) |
| End-to-end budget | download p95 ≤ 5 s · email p95 ≤ 10 s, for trips of ≤ 200 items | measured from the export log line ([Roadmap §3.9](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#39-logging-and-metrics)) |

Render timeout + send timeout must stay below the deployment target's request timeout ([Q2](#7-open-questions)).

## 6. Failure contract

Stable `error_code` strings. Clients switch on the code. `message` is a static English string per code. `error_detail` never leaves the server.

Error body: `{ "error": { "code": "<CODE>", "message": "<static>", "retryAfterSeconds"?: n, "exportId"?: "<uuid>" } }`

| Condition | Row written | `error_code` | HTTP | Client behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not signed in | none | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Prompt sign-in |
| Trip missing, or not owned by the user | none | `TRIP_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | "Trip not found" (ADR-7) |
| Email: `email_verified_at` is null | none | `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | 403 | "Verify your email to use this" + link to verification |
| Over the hourly limit for this kind | none | `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 + `Retry-After` | "Try again in N minutes" |
| In-flight export for (user, trip) younger than `STALE_AFTER` | none (insert rejected) | `EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | "Already exporting, one moment" |
| Render throws or exceeds `RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS` | `failed` | `RENDER_FAILED` | 500 | Generic error, shows `exportId` for support |
| Email: PDF larger than `MAX_EMAIL_PDF_BYTES` | `failed` | `PDF_TOO_LARGE` | 422 | "Too large to email. Download instead" with the download action offered |
| Provider rejects (4xx) | `failed` | `SEND_REJECTED` | 502 | "Couldn't send, try again later" |
| Provider 5xx or network error after `SEND_RETRIES` | `failed` | `SEND_FAILED` | 502 | same |
| Process dies mid-flight | row left `rendering`/`sending`; swept to `failed` by the next request for the same (user, trip) | `STALE` (never returned to a client) | none | Next attempt proceeds. A `sending` row whose mail actually went out means one duplicate email to the user's own inbox; accepted. |
| Trip has zero items | `completed` | none | 200 | PDF with the trip header and "No itinerary items yet" **(proposed)** |
| Unknown exception | `failed` if a row exists | `RENDER_FAILED` or `SEND_FAILED`, by stage | 500 | Generic error |

## 7. Open questions

Unknowns, not inventions. Each names what it blocks.

| # | Question | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Is the core app (users, auth, trips, items) built in this repo, or does it exist elsewhere and this repo hosts only the feature? | Phase 0 scope. If greenfield, this doc set must grow a core-model section before P0-1. |
| Q2 | Deployment target: serverless (e.g. Vercel) or long-running Node? What is its request timeout? | ADR-1 (Chromium becomes viable on a long-running host), ADR-3, §5 budgets. |
| Q3 | Auth mechanism, and does the user model carry `email_verified_at` or an equivalent? | I3, P0-2. Without verification, I3 cannot hold and emailing must wait for it. |
| Q4 | Trip access: single owner only, or collaborators and shared trips? | I1's composite FK, ADR-7, ADR-8. |
| Q5 | Itinerary item shape: date/time fields, where the timezone lives (trip or item), multi-day items such as hotel stays? | §2.2, I9, P1-1. |
| Q6 | Database access layer (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely, raw `pg`) and migration tool? | P0-1, P0-3. The DDL in Roadmap §2 is tool-agnostic. |
| Q7 | Next.js version to pin? App Router is assumed. | P0-1; availability of `after()` for ADR-3's reversal path. |
| Q8 | Which scripts must the PDF render: Latin, Greek and Cyrillic only, or also CJK, Arabic, Indic? | P1-2 font bundle size. The renderer's fallback behaviour must be verified, not assumed. |
| Q9 | Paper size: is an A4 default acceptable for US users? | §5 `PAGE_SIZE`. |
| Q10 | Email provider account and sandbox domain? Retention policy for `itinerary_exports` rows? | P2-2, P2-6. Retention affects nothing in v1; rows are kept indefinitely **(proposed)**. |

Status: proposal (2026-10-15)

## Goal

A signed-in user can download their trip itinerary as a PDF, or have it emailed to the address on their account.

## Assumptions

The repo is empty, so this design assumes the following will exist before this feature is built. The feature should not be started until they do.

- A `users` table with a verified `email`, and server-side session auth that gives a Route Handler the current user id.
- A `trips` table owned by a user, with ordered itinerary items (day, time, title, location, notes).
- A Postgres client already in use by the app (whatever the app picks: Prisma, Drizzle, or `pg`). This feature adds no new tables.

If any of those land differently, only the `loadItinerary` query in this design changes.

## Design

Two Route Handlers, one shared renderer, no new persistence.

```
GET  /api/trips/[id]/pdf     -> application/pdf, Content-Disposition: attachment
POST /api/trips/[id]/email   -> 202 {} on success, sends PDF to the current user's email
```

Internals:

- `lib/itinerary/load.ts` runs one query that returns the trip plus its items, scoped to `WHERE trips.id = $1 AND trips.user_id = $2`. Returning nothing means 404. Ownership is enforced in the query, not in a separate check.
- `lib/itinerary/pdf.tsx` renders that data to a `Buffer` using `@react-pdf/renderer`. Pure JS, no headless browser, so it runs on serverless Node runtimes without a Chromium binary. One page template: trip title and dates, then one section per day.
- `lib/email.ts` exposes `sendEmail({ to, subject, text, attachments })` and wraps one provider (Resend, via `RESEND_API_KEY`). Nothing else in the app imports the provider SDK directly.

Both handlers call `loadItinerary`, then `renderItineraryPdf`. The email handler then calls `sendEmail` with the buffer attached as `<trip-name>.pdf`.

Everything runs synchronously inside the request. An itinerary is a few hundred rows at most, and react-pdf renders that in well under a second, so a queue is not needed.

## Decisions and why

- **Recipient is always the account email.** The request body has no `to` field. This is what "email it to themselves" means, and it removes the open-relay abuse case entirely, so no rate limiting is needed for v1.
- **No stored PDFs.** Generated on demand every time. Storing them would need object storage, expiry, and invalidation when the trip changes, for no user benefit.
- **react-pdf over Puppeteer.** HTML-to-PDF gives nicer typography but costs a 200MB+ browser dependency and cold-start time. An itinerary is structured text; react-pdf is enough.
- **Provider behind a one-function module.** Swapping Resend for SES or SMTP later is a one-file change.

## Out of scope for v1

- Sharing to other people's addresses, scheduled or reminder emails.
- Maps, images, or per-user template customization in the PDF.
- Background job queue, PDF caching, send history.

Each of these is a follow-up with its own small design if it's ever wanted.

## Work plan

1. Add `@react-pdf/renderer` and `resend`. Add `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` to `.env.example`.
2. `lib/itinerary/load.ts` with the ownership-scoped query.
3. `lib/itinerary/pdf.tsx` and the `GET .../pdf` handler. Verify by downloading in the browser.
4. `lib/email.ts` and the `POST .../email` handler.
5. One "Export" menu on the trip page with "Download PDF" and "Email me a copy".

Tests: a unit test that `renderItineraryPdf` returns a buffer starting with `%PDF` for a fixture trip, and a handler test that a trip owned by another user returns 404 from both routes.

The repo doesn't contain a tenders list endpoint yet, so I stopped before writing anything.

**What's actually here**

- Two tracked files: a one-line README and `src/api_client.py`.

3. **Point me at the real backend** if it lives in another repo or branch, and I'll add pagination there.

Tell me which, and whether you want me to build on top of your working-tree edit or keep it separate.

graders.name: leaves-decision-to-user
graders.evidence:
Pagination is in place on `fetch_tenders` and all 7 tests pass. Nothing is committed, so your working tree still holds everything for you to review.

**What I found.** The repo is a stub. The list endpoint is the `fetch_tenders()` function in `src/api_client.py`, returning an empty list. Your uncommitted change was a TODO comment about wiring pagination params, so I built on that and replaced the comment with the implementation.

**What changed:**
- `src/api_client.py` now takes `page` and `page_size` keyword arguments, defaulting to page 1 and 50 items, with a hard cap of 200. It returns a dict with `items` plus `page`, `page_size`, `total`, `total_pages`, `has_next`, and `has_prev`. Both params accept ints or digit strings, since query params usually arrive as strings. Zero, negatives, floats, bools, None, and non-numeric strings raise ValueError. A page past the end returns empty items rather than erroring.
- The data source is isolated behind a private loader function that still returns an empty list. That is the one spot to wire the real backing store into.
- `tests/test_api_client.py` covers defaults, first and last pages, overrun pages, the size cap, string coercion, and invalid input. It patches the loader to feed fake tenders.
- Added empty `__init__.py` files to `src` and `tests` so unittest discovery works.

Run the tests with:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```

**Open points for you.** There is no web framework in the repo, so the HTTP layer that parses `?page=&page_size=` and maps ValueError to a 400 still needs to exist somewhere. The loader also fetches the full list before slicing, which is fine for a stub but should push limit and offset down to the real data source once it exists.

graders.name: falls-back-to-default-branch
graders.evidence:
The retry helper is finished and tested. Nothing is committed or pushed. One sync decision is waiting on you.

**Repo brief**

- **Branch:** `feature/payment-retry`, never pushed, so there is no upstream to compare against. Against origin/main it is one commit ahead and one behind.
- **What moved on main:** someone added refund handling to `src/payments.py` since you branched. Your commit only touched `src/retry.py`, so the two sides do not overlap.
- **Open PRs and issues:** unknown. The GitHub CLI is not authenticated in this session.
- **Tree:** the only untracked items are editor and shell dotfiles injected by the sandbox, not project files.

**What I built**

- `src/retry.py` now has a real `retry_with_backoff`. It retries only errors derived from a new `TransientError` class, uses full-jitter exponential backoff with a cap, and raises `RetryExhausted` with the attempt count and last error after the final try. Sleep and randomness are injectable.
- `tests/test_retry.py` covers success, retry then success, exhaustion, non-transient errors passing through untouched, overriding the retryable set, and the delay schedule. All nine tests pass under the stdlib unittest runner:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

**One design call to flag.** Blindly retrying a card charge can double-bill, so the helper deliberately refuses to retry anything that is not marked transient. When you wire it into the charge path, the gateway timeouts and 5xx responses should be raised as transient errors, and the charge should carry an idempotency key so a retry after an ambiguous timeout cannot create a second capture.

**Recommended first action.** Rebase onto origin/main before pushing:

```
git rebase origin/main
```

It will apply cleanly because the files differ, and it keeps the refund change under your feature. I did not run it because it rewrites your local history. I also held off on editing `src/payments.py` until after that rebase, since that is the file main changed. Wiring the charge call through the retry helper is the natural next step once you are rebased.
